## Rio, Paraty and a tropical island

Rio de Janeiro brings together the beaches of Copacabana, Ipanema and Leblon, forested mountains and a bay. Sugarloaf Mountain and Corcovado offer views over the city, and an evening at the Sambadrome is devoted to performances by samba schools.

Founded in 1667, Paraty grew through sugar cane cultivation, cachaça production and the shipment of gold from Minas Gerais to Portugal. Cobbled streets and historic churches preserve the town's colonial character. Tourists began to arrive after the Rio–Santos highway was built in the 1970s.

Around Angra dos Reis and Ilha Grande, boat trips pass green islands and bays with clear turquoise water. Spend two nights on Ilha Grande, with day 8 devoted to Lopes Mendes Beach.
